title: Linear AI agent for issue context and cycle reviews
h1: a linear bot that spots missing context before planning
description: Connect Linear to Dusk Bot for issue readiness, cycle checks and project updates. Copy routines that flag gaps without inventing priorities or owners.
answer: a bot in dusk bot can search linear issues, read comments and inspect cycles before helping you plan. give it a team and a small question, such as which issues lack enough detail to start. it can also create and update issues when allowed. use reading access for planning reports, and explicit ask-first instructions before granting tracker edits.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: better issue context before the planning call.

app.name: Linear
app.intro: issue status is only one part of readiness. the description may lack a clear outcome, or comments may contain an unresolved question. these actions let the bot gather that context without assuming it has authority over your team's priorities.

highlight.use: look for existing work before suggesting a new issue
read the full issue before assessing whether it is ready
find unanswered questions in the issue discussion
inspect the cycles for the team you named
learn the team's actual workflow states
collect project updates for a planning review
create an agreed issue from a prepared brief
apply a specified field change after you set the boundary

app.setup: add linear in **Connected apps**, complete linear's sign-in and allow your planning bot to use it. give the team name and a few issue references to establish the scope. explain what your ready and blocked states mean rather than asking the bot to guess from their names.

routines_intro: these routines look for possible duplicates, cycle questions and gaps in project communication. send one to your bot, then inspect its first few runs before expanding the scope.

routines.name: possible duplicate review
routines.message: every monday at 10, search the acme team issues for possible duplicates of the new issue briefs i supplied. compare descriptions and comments, not just titles. list candidate pairs with their issue references, matching details and differences. label uncertain matches for my review. do not create, merge, close or edit issues.
routines.output: candidate duplicate pairs with evidence to review

routines.name: cycle question list
routines.message: every thursday at 2, inspect the current cycle for the acme team and read the issues we marked blocked. group the blockers by the decision or input explicitly requested in their comments. mark unclear blockers as unclear. leave linear unchanged.
routines.output: a list of decisions needed before work can continue

routines.name: project update gaps
routines.message: every other tuesday at 4, read recent linear project updates for the projects i linked here. list projects with no update in the last two weeks, and questions that the latest update leaves open. do not publish a new update or edit a project.

asks:
creating an issue and changing its priority, owner or state are tracker changes. they may not ask first. keep a reviewer on read-only access so its findings cannot quietly change the plan.

if you want it to maintain issues later, restrict its action list and say "ask me before you change anything". posting a comment is a send, so it waits for **Allow** unless you've set a daily sending amount. creating a project update is an app change, not a send, so it may not ask first. keep it off the bot's list, or write "ask me before you change anything". one exception: a bot on **Full access** with no sending rule of its own may send up to 25 a day without asking, so give full-access bots **Ask every time** under sending.
cannot: assign work, change priority or create issues with a read-only linear permission. a suggested issue outline in dusk chat stays within a much smaller job.
know that a ticket is complete from its state name alone. ask for the description and comments behind a conclusion, and leave ambiguous readiness for a person to decide.
carry out a cycle review on a sleeping laptop. desktop routines need the app open; an always-on dusk cloud machine can perform the scheduled review while you are away.

sections.h: keep a blocker tied to its evidence
sections.md: tell the bot which states to inspect and ask it to point to the issue or comment behind every blocker. if implementation discussion lives in [github](/integrations/github), connect that source separately before asking for code context. a title that sounds similar is not enough to declare two issues duplicates.

sections.h: write the rule before allowing the update
sections.md: define the fields a routine may maintain and where missing values should be reported. a team decision in [notion](/integrations/notion) can supply context, but the bot should not turn an old note into a new priority without your instruction. [product managers](/for/product-managers) can use these small reviews around planning rather than delegating every tracker change.

faq.q: can i connect claude to linear without writing an mcp setup?
faq.a: you can choose claude or another ai for a bot in dusk bot and connect linear through **Connected apps**. a bot uses the composio actions listed here, so you don't set up a separate server.

faq.q: can the bot just tell me what is blocked?
faq.a: yes. grant reading access and ask it to inspect your blocked issues and their comments. give it the team and state names, and have it report the supporting context in chat.

faq.q: will issue creation ask me first?
faq.a: not by itself. creating an issue isn't a send, so it may not ask. include an explicit ask-first instruction and avoid granting create access to a bot that only needs to review.
